nodes.description: The 2026 preprint characterizes a C57BL/6J knock-in carrying a recurrent human H3-3A allele. Pups have delayed milestones and postnatal growth restriction; adult gait effects are more pronounced in males, while aged 60-week animals of both sexes have marked rotarod impairment. Nest-building and male aggression differ, but tested learning, memory and social preference are preserved. Brain histology was examined, with no genotype differences in the reported neuronal, astrocyte, Purkinje-cell or microglial counts. Gross brain endocast measures were also unchanged. This is partial phenotypic correspondence, not proof of a universal two-stage human course.

nodes.description: Yeast H3 mutants show separable defects: T45I and R83C permit cryptic intragenic transcription, while N108S traps FACT at gene 3-prime ends. Eight of nine newly tested mutants lack the FACT-trapping defect. Yeast native H3 expressed as the sole histone H3 source is a mechanistic surrogate, not a heterozygous human neuronal model. A114G is excluded from clinical variant inference because the study notes possible sequencing artifact.

nodes.description: The db1092 allele is D123N, not a homozygous null. Heterozygotes have variable craniofacial defects and homozygotes more severe losses. The 2020 glial experiment includes additional dominant-negative H3f3a RNA, producing a stronger perturbation. The original 2012 report found peripheral glia unaffected in its protocol. The allele is not a reported human patient allele and fish have five H3.3 genes.
